title: LSDE 2.4: turning off the built-in block properties a project doesn't use, and a "card" property for picking characters or items
author: djmisterjon
selftext:
I make LSDE, a dialogue, localization and narrative scene editor for games. Scenes are node graphs, and each block carries properties that the game reads at runtime.

**Version 2.4 changes two things in that graph:**

\- \*\*Native properties can be turned off.\*\* LSDE ships properties like delay or timeout on its blocks. A project that never uses timeout can now untick it, for one block type or for every block at once, and the block form stops offering it.

\- \*\*A new "card" property type.\*\* It holds one card (a character, an item, a place) picked from the categories you choose. On the block, the writer picks "Keycard" from a short list instead of typing an id.

The goal is a block form that only shows what the game reads, and values that can't be mistyped.

How do you keep the fields of your  dialogue tool in line with what your engine actually reads?
